The tools never returned any output here, so I didn't compute this with code. This answer comes from reading the text directly.

The passage that repeats most is the refrain that closes each of the seven letters to the churches: "ὁ ἔχων οὖς ἀκουσάτω τί τὸ πνεῦμα λέγει ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις" ("He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches"). It is 45 letters long and occurs 7 times, once each in the letters to Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia and Laodicea.

It cannot be extended in either direction and still occur 7 times:
- **Before it:** the letter preceding the passage differs between occurrences, for example "...misw|oexwn" versus "...zwhs|oexwn".
- **After it:** the next letter also differs: "t" (twnikwn), "o" (onikwn), "k" (kaitwaggelw) and "m" (metatauta).

Other repeated material in the text is either shorter than 40 letters or occurs fewer than 7 times. Examples are "eistousaiwnastwnaiwnwn" and the "xiliadesesfragismenoiekfulhs" formula in the list of the twelve tribes. I checked this by eye, not by an exhaustive search, so treat it as a confident manual result rather than a verified one.
